data.description:
## Description
**What**: Add a user-invoked `dso forbidden-action-override --reason="..."` command that grants a one-shot, audited override for the next blocked forbidden-action tool call, mirroring the sibling epic's dso commit-override audit-trail pattern. The agent cannot self-authorize; the override respects dso-fbky autonomous mode.
**Why**: A load-bearing block needs a sanctioned escape valve so a user can deliberately proceed past a HARD-GATE, with an audit record, without disabling the hook.
**Scope**:
- IN: The override CLI command, one-shot consumption semantics, an audit record capturing reason and timestamp, rejection of agent self-invocation, and dso-fbky autonomous-mode handling.
- OUT: The hook itself (draft-2); the registry (draft-1); abuse-detection surfacing at sprint Phase I or end-session closure.

## Done Definitions

- A user-invoked dso forbidden-action-override --reason="..." grants a single override that the next forbidden-action block consumes, after which a subsequent forbidden call is blocked again ← Satisfies: sc-3
- Each override writes an audit record capturing the supplied reason and a timestamp ← Satisfies: sc-3
- An override invocation that lacks a user context (agent self-authorization) is rejected and writes no override grant ← Satisfies: sc-3
- When this story is complete, under dso-fbky autonomous mode the override path follows the sibling epic's pattern and is not silently self-granted to the agent, verified by a test exercising the autonomous-mode path ← Satisfies: sc-3
- Unit tests written and passing for all new or modified logic, including one-shot consumption, audit-record write, and self-authorization rejection ← Satisfies: sc-3

## Considerations

- [Security] The override must reject agent self-authorization; only a user-invoked context grants it.
- [Security] Under dso-fbky autonomous mode the override is not self-granted to the agent; the autonomous-mode path mirrors the sibling epic's pattern.
- [External-blocker] Reuses the sibling-epic (d076-d35e, 750c-6033) dso commit-override audit-trail pattern and get_artifacts_dir() resolution; no in-epic depends_on is created for that outside infra.
- [Convention] Any new .sh file for the override command sets the executable bit (chmod +x) on creation.

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
data.title: As a user, I want a one-shot audited dso forbidden-action-override --reason="..." command, so I can authorize a blocked tool call once without the agent self-authorizing
